quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back at you in these conditions, creating glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: By law, every vehicle (except motorcycles) must have:

options.text: Brakes that never lock.
A foot brake and an emergency or parking brake.
A parking brake that can stop the vehicle within legal limits.

questions.correctAnswerText: A foot brake and an emergency or parking brake.
questions.explanation: The law requires all cars to have both a foot brake and a parking brake.

questions.question: You are in a turn lane ready to turn left. There is oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to get ready.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: For a second DUI conviction, the minimum jail sentence is:

options.text: Five days.
20 days.
45 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 days.
questions.explanation: A second DUI conviction carries a jail sentence of at least 45 days, up to 11 months and 29 days.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slow and unreliable.

questions.question: When turning left at a corner, yield to:

options.text: Other vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas and avoid the brakes. Do not try to stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are:

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what laws they must follow. They show rules about traffic direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking, and other situations. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green symbols.

questions.question: The traffic light turns red while you wait in the intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Back out of the intersection if you can.
Complete the turn when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the turn when it is safe.
questions.explanation: If you are in the intersection when the light changes, do not stop. Turn carefully when traffic clears. Always yield to oncoming traffic when turning left.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing back into your seat and resting your head on the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Grip the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic, drivers should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The roadway ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the road splits ahead. You must choose to turn either right or left.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate with traffic merging from on-ramps on your right, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Move to the left lane when traffic permits. This gives vehicles room to enter from the on-ramps on your right.

questions.question: For a first-time DUI conviction, the penalty is:

options.text: A $100 fine, 24 hours in jail, and a six-month license suspension.
A $500 fine, 12 hours in jail, and a three-month license suspension.
A $350 fine, 48 hours in jail, and a one-year license suspension.

questions.correctAnswerText: A $350 fine, 48 hours in jail, and a one-year license suspension.
questions.explanation: A first-time DUI conviction results in 48 hours in jail (or seven days if your blood alcohol level was 0.20 percent or higher), a fine between $350 and $1,500, and a one-year license suspension.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic on the road. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when some vehicles drive at different speeds than others.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid hard braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: In recent years, the number of fatal crashes involving alcohol in Tennessee has:

options.text: Increased.
Decreased.
Stayed the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decreased.
questions.explanation: In 2015, alcohol was involved in 34 percent of traffic deaths in Tennessee. In 2016, it was involved in about 27 percent.

questions.question: You can make a left turn at a red traffic light after stopping only if:

options.text: You are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlights' light.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead.
Keep instrument panel lights bright so others see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlights' light.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day. You cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small.
Honk your horn to move the motorcycle to the shoulder.
Have your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Do not share the same lane. Returning to the original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: Your car's rear end starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: When your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your car.

questions.question: You are entering a freeway. How should you check traffic?

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, use your side mirror and look over your shoulder. This helps you see traffic and avoid cars in your blind spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards ahead. Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and safe for turning on high-speed roads.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that haven't washed away yet. Drive extra carefully on wet roads.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where nearby vehicles are at all times.

questions.question: What does this sign warn about?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: You face a green light but traffic blocks the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection even if your light is green if traffic blocks your way. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light changes, you will block cross traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never pass or change lanes in an intersection. Before changing lanes elsewhere, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder and watch for other drivers trying to enter your lane.
